---
title: "Intermittent vs continuous infusion for β-lactams"
description: "How infusion mode reshapes the concentration–time curve and why fT>MIC simulations change when you move from bolus-like dosing to continuous infusion."
author: "Vahhab Piranfar"
date: "2026-10-17"
categories: [Learning, Antibiotic PK/PD]
---

For many β-lactams, the dominant index is **fT>MIC**. That makes **how you deliver the daily dose** a first-class modeling choice: short intermittent infusions create peaks and troughs; continuous infusion flattens the profile toward a steady free concentration.

::: {.callout-note}
## Scope
PK/PD geometry of infusion mode for simulation. Not a recommendation to change bedside practice.
:::

## Same daily dose, different shape

Hold clearance, volume, fu, and MIC fixed. Change only the input rate:

- **Intermittent**: repeated short infusions → oscillating $C_{\mathrm{free}}(t)$.
- **Extended infusion**: longer infusions per dose → higher troughs, softer peaks.
- **Continuous**: constant rate → approach to steady state $C_{\mathrm{ss,free}}$.

For a pure fT>MIC rule, continuous infusion often converts the question to whether $C_{\mathrm{ss,free}}$ stays above a multiple of MIC for the entire interval.

## What your simulator must not forget

1. **Loading dose** — continuous regimens often need an initial bolus; omitting it underestimates early fT>MIC.
2. **Stability / administration constraints** — model scenario ≠ pharmacy reality; label assumptions.
3. **Renal function** — Css moves with clearance; eGFR strata can dominate PTA differences more than infusion cosmetics.
4. **Targets as ratios** — some β-lactam analyses use $C_{\mathrm{ss,free}}/\mathrm{MIC} \ge 4$ (or similar) rather than raw T>MIC percent.

## Modeling comparison template

When you compare intermittent vs continuous:

- freeze the virtual population and MIC grid,
- change only the dosing input,
- report PTA curves on the same MIC axis,
- show early-interval behavior separately if loading doses differ.

## Takeaway

Infusion mode is not a plotting preference. It changes the **exposure geometry** that fT>MIC (and Css/MIC) rules evaluate.
